name: DeckCraft
summary: Edit PowerPoint presentations in Nextcloud with DeckCraft
description:
Open a PowerPoint (.pptx, .potx, .ppsx) or DeckCraft presentation in Files with **Edit in DeckCraft** and work on it right in the browser: themes, layouts, shapes, pictures, tables, charts, transitions, animations, speaker notes and the slide show.

- **Save** writes the presentation back in its own format (a .pptx stays a .pptx), and Nextcloud keeps the previous state as a file version.
- **Save As** stores it under a name and in a folder you pick, as PowerPoint or in DeckCraft's own format; later saves go to that file.
- **Export** (PDF, PNG, JPEG, outline) stores a file in any folder you pick.
- Read-only files open normally; saving offers a copy.
- If someone else changes the file while you have it open, you choose whether to replace their version or save a copy.
- Optionally, clicking a presentation in Files opens it in DeckCraft.
readme_features:
- **Edit in DeckCraft** appears in the Files action menu of every PowerPoint (.pptx, .potx, .ppsx) and DeckCraft (.deckcraft) presentation you can read.
- **Save** (Ctrl/⌘+S) writes the presentation back to Nextcloud in its own format (a .pptx stays a .pptx), and Nextcloud keeps the previous state as a file version.
- **Save As** (Ctrl/⌘+Shift+S) asks for a name and folder in your Nextcloud, as PowerPoint or in DeckCraft's own format (.deckcraft); later saves go to that file.
- **Export** (PDF, PNG, JPEG, outline) asks for a name and folder in your Nextcloud the first time.
bridge_notes: With `?host=parent`, DeckCraft starts with an empty presentation instead of the sample deck, an optional `&author=<name>` signs the user's comments, and the parent guards leaving the page with unsaved changes. Save sends the opened presentation back under its own name and format; Save As (`saveAs: true`) and a first Save of a presentation the parent never sent ask the parent where to keep it.
